items.title: Bernard Purdie interviewed by Monk Rowe, West Orange, New Jersey, July 30, 2003
items.q: Bucky saying one thing, George Duvivier saying something else and Bernard Purdie saying something else... If we’re not locked in it’s his job to stop it.

ctx.x: It doesn’t matter. The point is that a good producer is something that — he hears everything and only speaks when he needs to, and takes control when he has to. So he doesn’t have to worry about bending the rules or it gets out of hand with Bucky saying one thing, George Duvivier saying something else and Bernard Purdie saying something else. No. If we’re not locked in it’s his job to stop it. Let’s try it a different way. If he happens to be a player also, he knows. He is supposed to know what’s going to work…

And normally a producer will have — or maybe you can correct me if I’m wrong — but would a producer have been the person responsible for having those let’s say four individuals in that rhythm section there? Because he anticipates that they’re going to work well together?
